consequence.statement: New capability added to the validate command; evidence states no operational consequence for operators.

original.statement: The crossplane CLI (crank) validate command gains support for list input.

consequence.statement: An additive feature: crank validate now accepts list input. The release note describes only the new capability and mentions no failure, rejection or ignored setting, so an operator who does nothing is unaffected.

corrected.statement: The crank validate command gains support for list input. This is an additive, opt-in CLI capability, and an environment that does nothing sees no operational consequence.

decision.reason: [ev-d38f50d1a274] is a single changelog line, "feat(crank): add support for list input to validate". It describes only a new capability added to the crank validate command and says nothing about anything failing, being rejected or being ignored, so kind none (informational) holds for an environment that does nothing. However, the proposed statement says the evidence "states no operational consequence". It does not say that. The "none" is inferred from the change being purely additive, so I reworded the statement to match.
